housing.summary: Oulu has a comparatively affordable rental market versus Helsinki or Tampere, driven by a large student and tech-worker population (university and Nokia/technology hubs). Most rentals are unfurnished; leases are commonly open-ended or fixed-term. Deposits are typically one to two months' rent. Newcomers usually search via national rental portals or through student housing (PSOAS) if eligible.

banking.summary: Opening a Finnish bank account generally requires a Finnish personal identity code (henkilotunnus), a valid passport or national ID, a residence permit or proof of right to reside, and often a proof of address or employment contract. Strong electronic identification (online banking credentials) is central to daily life in Finland and is issued by the bank once the account is opened.
required_docs: Residence permit or proof of right to reside
Proof of address and/or employment contract

schools.summary: Public education in Oulu follows the Finnish national core curriculum and is free, including comprehensive school (grades 1-9). English-medium and international schooling is available for expatriate families, including an international programme in the city. Municipal early childhood education (day care) is also provided. Placement is coordinated by the City of Oulu education services.

legal_admin.summary: On arrival, foreign residents register with the Digital and Population Data Services Agency (DVV) to obtain a Finnish personal identity code (henkilotunnus) and to register their municipality of residence. EU/EEA citizens register their right of residence, while non-EU citizens first secure a residence permit from Migri (the Finnish Immigration Service). Registration underpins access to banking, healthcare, and tax services.
legal_admin.registration_step: Register with DVV to obtain a personal identity code (henkilotunnus) and register municipality of residence

tax_finance.summary: Income tax is administered by the Finnish Tax Administration (Vero). New workers must obtain a tax card (verokortti) specifying their withholding rate and provide it to their employer; without it, a higher default withholding applies. Non-residents may be taxed under separate rules. The personal identity code doubles as the individual's tax identifier.
tax_finance.tax_id_name: Henkilotunnus (personal identity code); tax card is verokortti

transport.summary: Oulu is known as a leading winter-cycling city with an extensive year-round cycling network, complemented by a municipal bus system covering the city and surrounding region. Single tickets and season/period passes are available via travel card and mobile app. Registered residents access public healthcare through the regional wellbeing services county after registering with a local health station.
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EEA licences are valid in Finland; many non-EU licences must be exchanged or a Finnish licence obtained, subject to bilateral recognition rules
transport.healthcare_registration: Register as a resident (via DVV) to access public primary care through the regional wellbeing services county / local health station
